links.comparator_used: RAG with LLM-based self-verification, within a four-configuration simulation that also included baseline LLM and RAG
links.outcome: Validation coverage, true-error recovery within covered claims, false-positive rate, reviewer correction rate, final document accuracy, and reviewer time
links.effect: Deterministic validator: covered 58.7 percent of claims, recovered 99.5 percent of errors within that coverage, 0.5 percent false-positive rate, reviewer correction rate 59.2 percent, final document accuracy 34.6 percent, reviewer time 10.0 minutes per document; self-verification: validation coverage 1.000, recovered 48.0 percent of true errors among checked claims, 8.1 percent false-positive rate, reviewer correction rate 44.6 percent, final document accuracy 16.1 percent, reviewer time 5.3 minutes per document
links.tradeoff: Narrower coverage and more reviewer time per document for the deterministic validator; reported limitations included parser brittleness, dependence on source-metadata currency, and risk of reduced reviewer vigilance.
links.quote: The deterministic validator covered a narrower 58.7 percent of claims but recovered 99.5 percent of errors within that coverage, with a 0.5 percent false-positive rate, and produced both the highest reviewer correction rate (59.2 percent versus 44.6 percent for self-verification) and the highest final document accuracy (34.6 percent versus 16.1 percent), despite requiring more reviewer time per document (10.0 versus 5.3 minutes).
